mechanism: Suppress only speculative begin-frame subscription for pending main-frame work, recent draw, and no-update commit in classic uncapped mode. Preserve actual redraw/main-frame/invalidation/video demand, pending-tree/tiles/smoothness requirements and all acknowledgements. Async commit/activation notifications re-evaluate actions and subscription, avoiding the fixed pacing delay on demanded frames.
feature: FlashwrightDemandDrivenUncappedFrames, default disabled; also require uncapped, asynchronous multi-threaded classic compositor without full-pipeline waits. Explicitly exclude SlimScheduler as well.

scope.workload: Unchanged original setup body, 15 tests per preflight capture and 240 per timed capture including warmup-labelled tests. Exact original outcomes and fixture request counts verified.
scope.reference: Same custom binary, feature off/on; no Playwright or fixed-pacing arm in this screen.
scope.policy: Existing renderer reuse, classic early-idle/uncapped scheduling, lazy VAAPI and locator cache off. No timer-pacing change. Original launch arguments checked before explicit private feature additions. Four-core quota, CPUs0–5, 8 GiB, swap0, Nice10.
scope.timing: Complete watchdog-owned fixture/runner/browser/shutdown interval, including natural observed drain; separate inner owner elapsed, charged cgroup CPU and peak memory retained.
scope.controls: Both arms pass three fresh storage/global contexts, moving-target trusted input, finite nondecreasing rAF timestamps, exact screenshot dimensions/pixels and live timer/idle-CPU observations.

nativeVerification.preScreen: 547 checks passed after correcting new test expectations; existing upstream tests unchanged.
nativeVerification.postScreen: Added explicit SlimScheduler exclusion inside existing mode-guard test and reran all547 successfully. No production source change or browser rerun.
nativeVerification.redControl: Nine of ten initial new checks fail on original source, exposing original speculative subscriptions. Additional reentrant and pipelined-commit checks were added with implementation.

retainedCorrection.reason: New copied reentrant tests incorrectly expected proactive subscription while a delivered main frame was pending, and incorrectly expected no subscription when repeated failed draws left another real main-frame request. Corrected expectations from source semantics and strengthened evidence of dispatched main-frame and resumed commit/draw. Initial failing results retained.

nativeVerification.scope: Actual scheduler observer removal/readdition, late commit and activation/draw, production main-frame-before-commit mode, abort/new request, successful and failed reentrant draw demand; state-machine required demand and six mode exclusions. Existing tests largely run feature off, not a complete enabled-policy regression matrix.

advancementRule: At least 10% lower complete time in both blocks at both worker counts and at least 20% lower charged CPU in both four-worker blocks, with all functional controls passing. If passed, run unchanged original application suites and broaden lifecycle/graphics/artifact checks before any adoption. Otherwise restore baseline; no unchanged parameter search.

decision.reason: All complete-time reductions fall below 10%; four-worker charged CPU reductions also fall below 20%.
decision.interpretation: Removing these speculative branches reduces some parallel work but does not reproduce the larger fixed-pacing CPU benefit. This does not identify why the remaining frames occur or show that other frame requests are unnecessary.

restoration.build: All three original source files restored with new mtime; headless_shell and cc_unittests rebuilt. Browser exactly reproduces original hash; original unit-executable hash was not recorded.

limitations: Two reversed blocks per worker count; no confidence interval, original application expansion or final nine-scenario acceptance.

No implementation clears or rewrites the history flags. Their retained lifetime until the next demanded frame can affect invalidation scheduling; dedicated enabled-policy history/invalidation coverage remains open.
Feature-enabled frame-sink loss, shutdown recovery, wider media/scroll/worklet/remote-frame behavior and artifact trace replay remain unverified.
The repeated-failed-draw control preserves outstanding real demand but does not drain every subsequent main-frame request through final idle.
Suppressed proactive work normally hides subscription round-trip latency. These selected functional tests do not establish all timing-sensitive behavior.
Original source and exact baseline browser are restored. The final test executable was rebuilt from restored sources; no pre-experiment unit-executable hash was recorded.
Input hashes and natural observed drain do not establish exhaustive resource/callback custody or release readiness.
